newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures extend rally as U.S. leads charge.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures extend rally as U.S. leads charge.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and gas oil futures extended early Wednesday gains as U.S. markets rallied strongly in response to fresh inventory data, brokers said.
Sept Brent crude gained 29 cents to $18.88 a barrel by 1411 GMT, with gas oil putting on $3.75 to $171.50 a tonne.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline was leading the charge after the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) released figures for last week showing nationwide stocks of the product fell by 3.5 million barrels.
DOE confirmation of the American Petroleum Institute (API)'s report of a big draw in crude stocks was adding to the momentum.
"There obviously been some help from gasoline but a big fund stop on WTI (NYMEX crude) at $20.20 was also hit," said a broker.
The API data, released late on Tuesday, showed U.S. crude stocks fell 9.7 million barrels last week, against expectations of a draw of about two million barrels.
Wednesday's DOE figures put the crude draw at an even heftier 9.9 million barrels.
But some brokers cast doubt on the reliability of the crude figures, given a repeat of the previous week's robust level of imports and a fall in average refinery operating rates.
"I think we could see Brent touch new highs for the session but it will probably be shortlived," said a broker.
Sept Brent broke through resistance at $18.85 to touch a session high of $18.90 shortly after NYMEX dealing began.
Brokers were also wary about progress towards a resumption of Iraqi exports under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
The U.N. was optimistic that its review of Iraq's aid distribution plan could be completed by the end of the week, spokesman Fred Eckhart said on Tuesday.
Some traders still believe Iraqi oil could be flowing again by the second half of August.
